location: Tasks > tests ("existing sequential/argv expectations updated"); Boundaries > Always > Child ("With >= 2 probed engines and no --sequential-browsers (direct runs included) it runs in parallel mode")
issue: Several existing unit tests call run_one_version with two engines and no sequential flag (tests/test-ps-e2e-run.py `_rov(["chromium", "firefox"])` at lines 325, 377, 397, 458 and 615). Under CAP-7 they enter parallel mode: snapshot-db through fl._exec, then real `--engine-worker` subprocesses. Those subprocesses do not see the in-process `drive_engine` stubs these tests install. One of them, "tanpa --sequential-browsers (run langsung): engine lain tetap jalan" (line 616), asserts in-process sequential semantics (`seen == ['chromium','firefox']`), which CAP-7 now contradicts. The spec names only CAP-3's Labels test as an expectation to update. It does not say whether these tests should add `sequential_browsers=True` (which changes what they cover: snapshot plus reset between engines) or go through the stubbed parallel driver.
implementation_impact: Running the current suite after the change either spawns real workers that try to launch Playwright, or fails/hangs. The implementer must decide test by test whether a test is about cell/timing shape (switch it to the stubbed parallel driver) or about in-process driving (add the flag, and accept snapshot/reset stubs). Done criterion 'no FAILED line' depends on that choice.
suggestion: List the affected tests in Tasks > tests and state the rule. For example: tests about cell/timing shape use the stubbed parallel driver. Line 615's check is rewritten to assert parallel mode (no in-process drive, workers spawned through the seam). Single-engine tests stay as they are.

location: Design Notes > Confirmation merge ("The version-level legacy fields (`findings`, `inconclusive`, `pass`, `browsers`, ... `skipped_browser`) are rebuilt from the final cells as today")
issue: "As today" is undefined for the new child-set cell states. Today `pass` = no findings in the driven engines, `browsers` = engines driven without launch_error, and `skipped_browser` = true when no engine drove. Consider a `parallel-unconfirmed` cell (findings [] with F in parallel_only), a `crash` cell (no result), or a `sequential-reset` cell (never driven). Taken literally, the rebuild gives `pass: true` for a version whose only finding could not be confirmed, or whose second engine crashed. With both workers crashed it gives `browsers: []`, which today's code reads as `skipped_browser: true`, as if no browser binary existed.
implementation_impact: The direct-run output (quickstart TDD loop, SKILL.md Lapis 4 direct runs) can show `pass: true` while the exit code is 1 and a finding went unconfirmed. The Honesty law says unconfirmable findings never pass silently. The implementer has to guess how each legacy field treats crash, parallel-unconfirmed and sequential-reset cells.
suggestion: Define the rebuild explicitly. `pass` = every cell's state is `pass` (or keep the old meaning, but also require no child-set inconclusive cell). `browsers` = engines whose cell was driven (a `browser:<engine>` phase exists). `skipped_browser` = true only when every probed engine had launch_error (never for crash or reset failures). Add one assertion for a parallel-unconfirmed version.

location: Design Notes > Phases ("`rerun-seq:<engine>` wraps the health check, reset and drive"); Design Notes > Snapshot and reset (health check = `_health_status` must be `healthy`); Tasks > docs (run-phases.md remediation: "check container health and the snapshot/reset lines of the progress log")
issue: The health check is not a phase, so a health failure writes no progress-log line of its own. The spec also never says what outcome `END rerun-seq:<engine>` (or the bare reset sequence before a BO-login fallback or a later sequential-fallback engine) carries when the routine fails and the drive is skipped. `fl.phase` writes `ok` unless `ph.status` is set or an exception escapes. So a health failure can show up in the log only as `END rerun-seq:chromium ok` with no reset lines. The docs then tell the operator to find the cause in 'the snapshot/reset lines of the progress log', and run-phases.md 'Sebab infra per versi V' says to name the cause 'dari stderr dan log kemajuan'.
implementation_impact: The implementer must guess whether the health check gets its own phase (which would change `boot_phases` and the I/O rows' expected phase lists), whether `rerun-seq` END gets a failure status, and whether anything goes to stderr. The operator-facing remediation can point at lines that do not exist.
suggestion: State that a failed reset routine sets the wrapping phase's status (e.g. `END rerun-seq:<engine> parallel-unconfirmed(<sub-phase>)`) and prints one stderr line with the cell `errors` entry. Keep the health check out of `boot_phases` (as the I/O rows assume), and have the docs point to that END line and stderr.

location: Design Notes > Confirmation merge ("BO-login fallback: `findings` and `inconclusive` are that pass's alone"; "`parallel_only` = `[]` ... unless filled above")
issue: Take an engine that gets the BO-login fallback, whose discarded parallel pass had a finding F (for example an FO step) that the fallback pass does not reproduce. F vanishes: it is not in `findings`, and `parallel_only` is filled only for rerun-seq and parallel-unconfirmed cells. An engine that got `rerun-seq` instead records the same kind of non-reproduced finding in `parallel_only`. Meanwhile the same discarded F is counted as 'a finding in any engine's parallel pass' and forces other engines to rerun. So it is treated as real evidence for others but not kept for its own cell. (Round 3 noted only the sub-case where the fallback pass fails to launch.)
implementation_impact: The implementer cannot tell whether the omission is intended. Tests for the 'BO-login fallback' row cannot assert `parallel_only` for this case, and the operator loses the only trace of a parallel-only observation that made sibling engines rerun.
suggestion: Say explicitly that a fallback engine's discarded parallel findings whose (scenario, step, action) is absent from the fallback pass's findings go to `parallel_only`, as for a rerun. Or say explicitly that they are dropped, and why. Add the case to the 'BO-login fallback' I/O row.

location: Design Notes > `scenario_spans` ("after the last step's marker the worker leaves `browser:<engine>` with no barrier wait"); I/O row 'Parallel clean' ("`started_at`/`finished_at` overlap"); SPEC CAP-7 success ("both start before either ends")
issue: With no barrier wait after the last step, overlap of the two `browser:<engine>` phases is guaranteed only when the driven list has at least 2 steps. With 2 or more steps, an engine cannot pass step 0's barrier before the other engine has written its step-0 marker. A module with only the universal smoke has one step (BO, so LOCK_EX). There engine A can take the lock, finish, write marker 0 and leave its browser phase before engine B's worker has even started its `browser:` phase (slow interpreter start or browser launch). Then max(started_at) > min(finished_at). The I/O row states overlap unconditionally.
implementation_impact: A stub test for 'Parallel clean' or AC1 that uses a smoke-only scenario list can be flaky or fail. The implementer has to guess whether the overlap claim needs a final barrier (as the contract's Lockstep mechanism literally describes: 'then waits until that file exists for every other engine') or whether it is limited to lists of 2 or more steps.
suggestion: Either keep a final barrier wait inside `browser:<engine>` (which matches the contract mechanism and guarantees overlap), or limit the overlap claim in 'Parallel clean' and AC1 to driven lists of 2 or more steps and require the unit/stub tests to use at least two scenarios.

location: Boundaries > Always > Child (worker `crash` cell); ps-run-layer `_on_reaped` (`if any(r["reason"] == "crash" ...): self.keep = True`); Design Notes > Worker interface (work dir deleted in the version process's `finally`)
issue: ps-run-layer keeps its temp dir 'for diagnosis' whenever any appended record has reason `crash`, which it assumes comes from an unreadable child output. Under CAP-7 the child itself emits `crash` cells for workers. ps-run-layer will then retain the child's perfectly readable `-o` output and log 'bukti per-versi DIPERTAHANKAN untuk diagnosis'. Meanwhile the version process has deleted the worker's spec.json and work dir, the only worker-side artifacts. A partial result file would have been there too, but a crash means no parseable result. The spec says nothing about this interaction.
implementation_impact: The implementer must decide whether child-set `crash` cells should trigger `keep`, and whether a crashed worker's work dir should be kept. Either choice is a guess, and the operator gets a misleading diagnosis message.
suggestion: State that `keep` stays tied to ps-run-layer-written `crash` records only (child output unreadable), not child-set ones. Also state where a worker crash can be diagnosed: stderr is inherited, so the child's stderr, plus `browser_notes` with the exit code. Optionally keep the work dir when a worker crashed.

location: Boundaries > Never ("the reset routine is written so CAP-5 can reuse it, but no warm path exists") vs cell-contract.md > Warm container > Reset per iteration
issue: 'Written so CAP-5 can reuse it' is a constraint with no testable criterion, and the two resets differ in the contract. The CAP-5 baseline is taken after `wait-healthy` and before the first install. CAP-5's `reset-files` has no module copy, and each iteration then runs `install`. CAP-7's snapshot is taken after `warmup-bo` (installed state), and its `reset-files` ends with `cp -r /ps-module-src` and no install. The spec does not say which parts must be parameterized: the snapshot file names, the module-copy step, or the wait-http/warmup-bo tail.
implementation_impact: The implementer must guess the routine's interface (flags or parameters for 'copy module', 'snapshot paths', 'tail phases'). A reviewer cannot check the constraint, and CAP-5 may still have to refactor it.
suggestion: Either drop the sentence, or name the seam. For example: `reset_routine(session, mod_name, *, snapshot=('/tmp/psm-e2e-snapshot.sql', '/tmp/psm-e2e-snapshot.files'), copy_module=True, tail=True)`, where CAP-7 always passes the defaults. Do not add any test for the CAP-5 variants.
